note: Narration for the Sejarah kids stories (sej-k, sej-k-m, sej-k-h, sej-k-x; MODULES_LEVELS_STORIES.md section 5). One clip per story panel; the text is the panel caption spoken for a 7-12-year-old (numbers in words). Voice: the shared English adult voice in voices.json, warm and unhurried, storytelling pace. A reviewer listens to every clip; names of foreign people and places follow the per-clip note. Generated by scratchpad/fu12/sej_k/gen.py; edit the generator, not this file.

clips.text: Ki Hajar Dewantara was born in Yogyakarta in 1889. His childhood name was Soewardi.
clips.note: ST-KI-HAJAR panel 1 (sej-k). Say 'Soewardi' as Suwardi; 'Tut Wuri Handayani' in Javanese: tut wu-ri han-da-ya-ni.

clips.text: Back then, Indonesia was ruled by the Dutch. Only a few Indonesian children could go to school.
clips.note: ST-KI-HAJAR panel 2 (sej-k). Say 'Soewardi' as Suwardi; 'Tut Wuri Handayani' in Javanese: tut wu-ri han-da-ya-ni.

clips.text: In 1922 he founded the Taman Siswa school in Yogyakarta. There, Indonesian children could learn.
clips.note: ST-KI-HAJAR panel 3 (sej-k). Say 'Soewardi' as Suwardi; 'Tut Wuri Handayani' in Javanese: tut wu-ri han-da-ya-ni.

clips.text: His motto, "Tut Wuri Handayani", means a teacher encourages from behind. It is on the logo of Indonesian education.
clips.note: ST-KI-HAJAR panel 4 (sej-k). Say 'Soewardi' as Suwardi; 'Tut Wuri Handayani' in Javanese: tut wu-ri han-da-ya-ni.

clips.text: Today his birthday, 2 May, is National Education Day. Every child has the right to learn!
clips.note: ST-KI-HAJAR panel 5 (sej-k). Say 'Soewardi' as Suwardi; 'Tut Wuri Handayani' in Javanese: tut wu-ri han-da-ya-ni.

clips.text: Kartini was born in Jepara, Central Java, in 1879. She loved to learn.
clips.note: ST-KARTINI panel 1 (sej-k). 'Habis Gelap Terbitlah Terang' is the book title; read it as a title, not a sentence.

clips.text: When she was 12, Kartini had to leave school and stay at home. That was the custom for noble girls at the time.
clips.note: ST-KARTINI panel 2 (sej-k). 'Habis Gelap Terbitlah Terang' is the book title; read it as a title, not a sentence.

clips.text: Kartini kept reading and wrote letters to her friends in the Netherlands. She wanted girls to go to school too.
clips.note: ST-KARTINI panel 3 (sej-k). 'Habis Gelap Terbitlah Terang' is the book title; read it as a title, not a sentence.

clips.text: In 1903 Kartini opened a small school for girls. She taught there herself.
clips.note: ST-KARTINI panel 4 (sej-k). 'Habis Gelap Terbitlah Terang' is the book title; read it as a title, not a sentence.

clips.text: After Kartini died, her letters became a book, Habis Gelap Terbitlah Terang (After Darkness Comes Light). Every 21 April we celebrate Kartini Day.
clips.note: ST-KARTINI panel 5 (sej-k). 'Habis Gelap Terbitlah Terang' is the book title; read it as a title, not a sentence.

clips.text: Florence Nightingale was born in Italy in 1820 and grew up in England. She wanted to care for sick people.
clips.note: ST-NIGHTINGALE panel 1 (sej-k). Say 'Nightingale' in English (NAIT-ing-gayl); 'Florence' as in English.

clips.text: In 1854 she and 38 nurses went to an army hospital in Turkey. The hospital was dirty, and many patients were very ill.
clips.note: ST-NIGHTINGALE panel 2 (sej-k). Say 'Nightingale' in English (NAIT-ing-gayl); 'Florence' as in English.

clips.text: Florence and the nurses cleaned the hospital and prepared food. The patients were cared for much better.
clips.note: ST-NIGHTINGALE panel 3 (sej-k). Say 'Nightingale' in English (NAIT-ing-gayl); 'Florence' as in English.

clips.text: At night she walked around with a lamp to check on the patients. People called her "the Lady with the Lamp".
clips.note: ST-NIGHTINGALE panel 4 (sej-k). Say 'Nightingale' in English (NAIT-ing-gayl); 'Florence' as in English.

clips.text: In 1860 she opened a school for nurses in London. Now her birthday, 12 May, is International Nurses Day.
clips.note: ST-NIGHTINGALE panel 5 (sej-k). Say 'Nightingale' in English (NAIT-ing-gayl); 'Florence' as in English.

clips.text: From Florence we learn to care for sick people and to keep things clean.
clips.note: ST-NIGHTINGALE panel 6 (sej-k). Say 'Nightingale' in English (NAIT-ing-gayl); 'Florence' as in English.

clips.text: Dewi Sartika was born in West Java in 1884. As a child, she loved playing school.
clips.note: ST-DEWI-SARTIKA panel 1 (sej-k). 'Sakola Istri' is Sundanese (sa-KO-la IS-tri).

clips.text: She taught the children around her to read and write. Her board was made of wood, and her chalk was charcoal!
clips.note: ST-DEWI-SARTIKA panel 2 (sej-k). 'Sakola Istri' is Sundanese (sa-KO-la IS-tri).

clips.text: In those days, many girls could not go to school. Dewi Sartika wanted them to learn and to stand on their own feet.
clips.note: ST-DEWI-SARTIKA panel 3 (sej-k). 'Sakola Istri' is Sundanese (sa-KO-la IS-tri).

clips.text: On 16 January 1904 she opened Sakola Istri in Bandung, a school for girls. The pupils learned reading, arithmetic and sewing.
clips.note: ST-DEWI-SARTIKA panel 4 (sej-k). 'Sakola Istri' is Sundanese (sa-KO-la IS-tri).

clips.text: Her schools spread to many towns in West Java. Today Dewi Sartika is a National Hero of Indonesia.
clips.note: ST-DEWI-SARTIKA panel 5 (sej-k). 'Sakola Istri' is Sundanese (sa-KO-la IS-tri).

clips.text: From Dewi Sartika we learn to share what we know with others.
clips.note: ST-DEWI-SARTIKA panel 6 (sej-k). 'Sakola Istri' is Sundanese (sa-KO-la IS-tri).

clips.text: Zheng He, also called Cheng Ho, was born in China around 1371. He became an admiral, a leader of sailors.
clips.note: ST-ZHENG-HE panel 1 (sej-k). Say 'Zheng He' as JUNG-huh; 'Cheng Ho' as in Indonesian; 'Sam Poo Kong' as in Indonesian.

clips.text: From 1405 he led seven great voyages. On the first voyage there were more than 200 ships!
clips.note: ST-ZHENG-HE panel 2 (sej-k). Say 'Zheng He' as JUNG-huh; 'Cheng Ho' as in Indonesian; 'Sam Poo Kong' as in Indonesian.

clips.text: His ships sailed to Southeast Asia, India, Arabia and Africa. They found their way with a compass and the stars.
clips.note: ST-ZHENG-HE panel 3 (sej-k). Say 'Zheng He' as JUNG-huh; 'Cheng Ho' as in Indonesian; 'Sam Poo Kong' as in Indonesian.

clips.text: He also stopped in Java and Sumatra to trade and make friends. In Semarang, the Sam Poo Kong temple remembers his visit.
clips.note: ST-ZHENG-HE panel 4 (sej-k). Say 'Zheng He' as JUNG-huh; 'Cheng Ho' as in Indonesian; 'Sam Poo Kong' as in Indonesian.

clips.text: Zheng He's voyages linked many peoples. We learn to be brave explorers and friends to everyone.
clips.note: ST-ZHENG-HE panel 5 (sej-k). Say 'Zheng He' as JUNG-huh; 'Cheng Ho' as in Indonesian; 'Sam Poo Kong' as in Indonesian.

clips.text: Ibn Battuta was born in Tangier, Morocco, in 1304. He loved learning and wanted to see the world.
clips.note: ST-IBN-BATTUTA panel 1 (sej-k). Say 'Ibn Battuta' as ib-nu ba-TU-ta; 'Rihlah' as RIH-lah; 'Samudera Pasai' as in Indonesian.

clips.text: In 1325, at the age of 21, he set off on the pilgrimage to Mecca. He travelled with a camel caravan.
clips.note: ST-IBN-BATTUTA panel 2 (sej-k). Say 'Ibn Battuta' as ib-nu ba-TU-ta; 'Rihlah' as RIH-lah; 'Samudera Pasai' as in Indonesian.

clips.text: He kept travelling for almost 30 years, to Africa, India, China and Sumatra. That's about 120,000 kilometres!
clips.note: ST-IBN-BATTUTA panel 3 (sej-k). Say 'Ibn Battuta' as ib-nu ba-TU-ta; 'Rihlah' as RIH-lah; 'Samudera Pasai' as in Indonesian.

clips.text: In Sumatra he stopped at the kingdom of Samudera Pasai around 1345. He was welcomed as the sultan's guest.
clips.note: ST-IBN-BATTUTA panel 4 (sej-k). Say 'Ibn Battuta' as ib-nu ba-TU-ta; 'Rihlah' as RIH-lah; 'Samudera Pasai' as in Indonesian.

clips.text: Back home, he told the story of his travels, and a writer wrote it down. The book is called the Rihla, which means "journey".
clips.note: ST-IBN-BATTUTA panel 5 (sej-k). Say 'Ibn Battuta' as ib-nu ba-TU-ta; 'Rihlah' as RIH-lah; 'Samudera Pasai' as in Indonesian.

clips.text: Thanks to his book, we know what the world was like almost 700 years ago. We learn to be curious and to write down what we see.
clips.note: ST-IBN-BATTUTA panel 6 (sej-k). Say 'Ibn Battuta' as ib-nu ba-TU-ta; 'Rihlah' as RIH-lah; 'Samudera Pasai' as in Indonesian.

clips.text: Marie Curie was born in Warsaw, Poland, in 1867. At that time, women were not allowed to study at the university in Warsaw.
clips.note: ST-CURIE panel 1 (sej-k-m). Say 'Curie' as KYUR-ee (English) / KÜ-ri (Indonesian); 'Warsawa' as in Indonesian.

clips.text: In 1891 she moved to Paris, France, to study. She worked hard at physics and mathematics.
clips.note: ST-CURIE panel 2 (sej-k-m). Say 'Curie' as KYUR-ee (English) / KÜ-ri (Indonesian); 'Warsawa' as in Indonesian.

clips.text: With her husband, Pierre Curie, she studied rocks that gave off invisible rays. In 1898 they discovered two new elements: polonium and radium.
clips.note: ST-CURIE panel 3 (sej-k-m). Say 'Curie' as KYUR-ee (English) / KÜ-ri (Indonesian); 'Warsawa' as in Indonesian.

clips.text: She named polonium after her homeland, Poland. Marie was the first woman to win a Nobel Prize, and she won it twice!
clips.note: ST-CURIE panel 4 (sej-k-m). Say 'Curie' as KYUR-ee (English) / KÜ-ri (Indonesian); 'Warsawa' as in Indonesian.

clips.text: Today we know radium is dangerous, so scientists work with protection. From Marie Curie we learn to be patient, careful and full of questions.
clips.note: ST-CURIE panel 5 (sej-k-m). Say 'Curie' as KYUR-ee (English) / KÜ-ri (Indonesian); 'Warsawa' as in Indonesian.

clips.text: Ibn al-Haytham was born in Basra, Iraq, around 965. Later he lived for many years in Cairo, Egypt.
clips.note: ST-IBN-HAYTHAM panel 1 (sej-k-m). Say 'Ibn al-Haytham' as ib-nul hai-TSAM; 'Kitab Optik' as in Indonesian.

clips.text: Long ago, many people thought our eyes sent out rays so that we could see. Ibn al-Haytham wanted to test whether that was true.
clips.note: ST-IBN-HAYTHAM panel 2 (sej-k-m). Say 'Ibn al-Haytham' as ib-nul hai-TSAM; 'Kitab Optik' as in Indonesian.

clips.text: He experimented in a dark room with a small hole. Light came in through the hole and made an upside-down picture on the wall.
clips.note: ST-IBN-HAYTHAM panel 3 (sej-k-m). Say 'Ibn al-Haytham' as ib-nul hai-TSAM; 'Kitab Optik' as in Indonesian.

clips.text: He showed that we see because light from objects enters our eyes. He wrote all his experiments in his Book of Optics.
clips.note: ST-IBN-HAYTHAM panel 4 (sej-k-m). Say 'Ibn al-Haytham' as ib-nul hai-TSAM; 'Kitab Optik' as in Indonesian.

clips.text: Glasses and cameras use the science of light that he studied. From Ibn al-Haytham we learn to test an idea before we believe it.
clips.note: ST-IBN-HAYTHAM panel 5 (sej-k-m). Say 'Ibn al-Haytham' as ib-nul hai-TSAM; 'Kitab Optik' as in Indonesian.

clips.text: Wilbur and Orville Wright were brothers from the United States. As boys, they built copies of a toy helicopter their father gave them.
clips.note: ST-WRIGHT panel 1 (sej-k-m). Say 'Wright' as RAIT; 'Kitty Hawk' and 'Dayton' in English.

clips.text: In 1892 they opened a bicycle shop in the town of Dayton. They were good at repairing and building bicycles.
clips.note: ST-WRIGHT panel 2 (sej-k-m). Say 'Wright' as RAIT; 'Kitty Hawk' and 'Dayton' in English.

clips.text: They watched birds fly, then tested wings with kites and a wind tunnel. They tried again and again.
clips.note: ST-WRIGHT panel 3 (sej-k-m). Say 'Wright' as RAIT; 'Kitty Hawk' and 'Dayton' in English.

clips.text: On 17 December 1903, near Kitty Hawk, Orville flew a plane with an engine for 12 seconds. It was the first successful powered aeroplane flight.
clips.note: ST-WRIGHT panel 4 (sej-k-m). Say 'Wright' as RAIT; 'Kitty Hawk' and 'Dayton' in English.

clips.text: That day Wilbur also flew, for 59 seconds. Thanks to their teamwork and patience, planes now fly all over the world.
clips.note: ST-WRIGHT panel 5 (sej-k-m). Say 'Wright' as RAIT; 'Kitty Hawk' and 'Dayton' in English.

clips.text: Louis Braille was born in the village of Coupvray, France, in 1809. His father made saddles and harnesses for horses.
clips.note: ST-BRAILLE panel 1 (sej-k-m). Say 'Louis Braille' in French-ish: lu-I BRAI; 'Coupvray' as ku-VRÉ.

clips.text: When he was 3, Louis hurt his eye in an accident in his father's workshop. From the age of 5, he could not see.
clips.note: ST-BRAILLE panel 2 (sej-k-m). Say 'Louis Braille' in French-ish: lu-I BRAI; 'Coupvray' as ku-VRÉ.

clips.text: At 10, he went to a school for blind children in Paris. Its books had big raised letters that were heavy and hard to read by touch.
clips.note: ST-BRAILLE panel 3 (sej-k-m). Say 'Louis Braille' in French-ish: lu-I BRAI; 'Coupvray' as ku-VRÉ.

clips.text: At about 15, Louis made letters out of six raised dots. These dot letters are easy to feel, and blind people can write them too.
clips.note: ST-BRAILLE panel 4 (sej-k-m). Say 'Louis Braille' in French-ish: lu-I BRAI; 'Coupvray' as ku-VRÉ.

clips.text: Today braille is used all over the world, and his birthday, 4 January, is World Braille Day. We learn that everyone has the right to read.
clips.note: ST-BRAILLE panel 5 (sej-k-m). Say 'Louis Braille' in French-ish: lu-I BRAI; 'Coupvray' as ku-VRÉ.

clips.text: Al-Khwarizmi lived about 1,200 years ago in Baghdad, a great city in Iraq. He was a master of mathematics and the stars.
clips.note: ST-KHWARIZMI panel 1 (sej-k-h). Say 'Al-Khwarizmi' as al-khwa-RIZ-mi; 'Baitul Hikmah' as in Indonesian/Arabic.

clips.text: He worked at the House of Wisdom. There, scholars translated and wrote books from many peoples.
clips.note: ST-KHWARIZMI panel 2 (sej-k-h). Say 'Al-Khwarizmi' as al-khwa-RIZ-mi; 'Baitul Hikmah' as in Indonesian/Arabic.

clips.text: He wrote a book about the digits 0 to 9 from India. With those ten digits, arithmetic became much easier.
clips.note: ST-KHWARIZMI panel 3 (sej-k-h). Say 'Al-Khwarizmi' as al-khwa-RIZ-mi; 'Baitul Hikmah' as in Indonesian/Arabic.

clips.text: Another of his books, al-Jabr, taught how to find an unknown number. That is where the word "algebra" comes from.
clips.note: ST-KHWARIZMI panel 4 (sej-k-h). Say 'Al-Khwarizmi' as al-khwa-RIZ-mi; 'Baitul Hikmah' as in Indonesian/Arabic.

clips.text: His maths was used to measure land and share inheritances fairly. Even the word "algorithm" comes from his name!
clips.note: ST-KHWARIZMI panel 5 (sej-k-h). Say 'Al-Khwarizmi' as al-khwa-RIZ-mi; 'Baitul Hikmah' as in Indonesian/Arabic.

clips.text: Ibn Sina was born in 980 near Bukhara, in today's Uzbekistan. From childhood he learned very fast.
clips.note: ST-IBN-SINA panel 1 (sej-k-h). Say 'Ibn Sina' as ib-nu SI-na; 'Al-Qanun fi al-Tibb' as al-qa-NUN fit-TIB; 'Avicenna' a-vi-SEN-na.

clips.text: He read medical books and tried to treat sick people. By the age of 18, he was already a doctor.
clips.note: ST-IBN-SINA panel 2 (sej-k-h). Say 'Ibn Sina' as ib-nu SI-na; 'Al-Qanun fi al-Tibb' as al-qa-NUN fit-TIB; 'Avicenna' a-vi-SEN-na.

clips.text: When he cured the ruler of Bukhara, he was allowed to read in the palace library. He read almost every book in it!
clips.note: ST-IBN-SINA panel 3 (sej-k-h). Say 'Ibn Sina' as ib-nu SI-na; 'Al-Qanun fi al-Tibb' as al-qa-NUN fit-TIB; 'Avicenna' a-vi-SEN-na.

clips.text: He wrote the Canon of Medicine, a great book about illnesses, medicines and healthy living. Doctors in Asia and Europe used it for hundreds of years.
clips.note: ST-IBN-SINA panel 4 (sej-k-h). Say 'Ibn Sina' as ib-nu SI-na; 'Al-Qanun fi al-Tibb' as al-qa-NUN fit-TIB; 'Avicenna' a-vi-SEN-na.

clips.text: A crater on the Moon is named Avicenna, his Latin name. From Ibn Sina we learn to love reading and to help the sick.
clips.note: ST-IBN-SINA panel 5 (sej-k-h). Say 'Ibn Sina' as ib-nu SI-na; 'Al-Qanun fi al-Tibb' as al-qa-NUN fit-TIB; 'Avicenna' a-vi-SEN-na.

clips.text: Mohammad Hatta was born in Bukittinggi, West Sumatra, in 1902. He loved reading from an early age.
clips.note: ST-HATTA panel 1 (sej-k-h). 'Bung Hatta' as in Indonesian; 'Sjahrir' = Syahrir.

clips.text: He studied economics in the Netherlands. There he learned about cooperatives, businesses owned together by their members.
clips.note: ST-HATTA panel 2 (sej-k-h). 'Bung Hatta' as in Indonesian; 'Sjahrir' = Syahrir.

clips.text: Because he fought for independence, the Dutch government exiled him far away. He took sixteen chests of books with him!
clips.note: ST-HATTA panel 3 (sej-k-h). 'Bung Hatta' as in Indonesian; 'Sjahrir' = Syahrir.

clips.text: On the island of Banda Neira, he and his friend Sjahrir ran an afternoon school for the island's children.
clips.note: ST-HATTA panel 4 (sej-k-h). 'Bung Hatta' as in Indonesian; 'Sjahrir' = Syahrir.

clips.text: On 17 August 1945, he and Soekarno proclaimed Indonesia's independence. Hatta became the first Vice President.
clips.note: ST-HATTA panel 5 (sej-k-h). 'Bung Hatta' as in Indonesian; 'Sjahrir' = Syahrir.

clips.text: He encouraged people to start cooperatives so they could get ahead together. That is why he is called the Father of Indonesian Cooperatives.
clips.note: ST-HATTA panel 6 (sej-k-h). 'Bung Hatta' as in Indonesian; 'Sjahrir' = Syahrir.

clips.text: B.J. Habibie was born in Parepare, South Sulawesi, in 1936. As a boy he loved reading and asking how things work.
clips.note: ST-HABIBIE panel 1 (sej-k-h). Say 'N250' as 'N dua lima puluh' (id) / 'N-two-fifty' (en); 'Aachen' as A-khen.

clips.text: He studied aircraft engineering in Aachen, Germany, and earned a doctorate. Then he worked at an aircraft factory there.
clips.note: ST-HABIBIE panel 2 (sej-k-h). Say 'N250' as 'N dua lima puluh' (id) / 'N-two-fifty' (en); 'Aachen' as A-khen.

clips.text: In 1974 he came home to Indonesia. He led the aircraft factory in Bandung and trained many young engineers.
clips.note: ST-HABIBIE panel 3 (sej-k-h). Say 'N250' as 'N dua lima puluh' (id) / 'N-two-fifty' (en); 'Aachen' as A-khen.

clips.text: On 10 August 1995, the N-two-fifty Gatotkaca, designed in Indonesia, made its first flight in Bandung. People cheered with joy.
clips.note: ST-HABIBIE panel 4 (sej-k-h). Say 'N250' as 'N dua lima puluh' (id) / 'N-two-fifty' (en); 'Aachen' as A-khen.

clips.text: Today 10 August is National Technology Awakening Day. From Habibie we learn to dream big and keep learning.
clips.note: ST-HABIBIE panel 5 (sej-k-h). Say 'N250' as 'N dua lima puluh' (id) / 'N-two-fifty' (en); 'Aachen' as A-khen.

clips.text: Helen Keller was born in Alabama, in the United States, in 1880. As a baby she fell very ill, and afterwards she could not see or hear.
clips.note: ST-KELLER panel 1 (sej-k-x). Say 'Helen Keller' and 'Anne Sullivan' in English; spell 'a-i-r' letter by letter (id) and 'w-a-t-e-r' (en).

clips.text: Little Helen found it hard to tell people what she wanted. She was often sad and upset because no one understood.
clips.note: ST-KELLER panel 2 (sej-k-x). Say 'Helen Keller' and 'Anne Sullivan' in English; spell 'a-i-r' letter by letter (id) and 'w-a-t-e-r' (en).

clips.text: In 1887 a teacher, Anne Sullivan, arrived and spelled words with her fingers into Helen's palm. By the water pump, Helen finally understood: w-a-t-e-r!
clips.note: ST-KELLER panel 3 (sej-k-x). Say 'Helen Keller' and 'Anne Sullivan' in English; spell 'a-i-r' letter by letter (id) and 'w-a-t-e-r' (en).

clips.text: Helen learned to read braille and to write. In 1904 she graduated from university, the first deaf-blind person ever to do so.
clips.note: ST-KELLER panel 4 (sej-k-x). Say 'Helen Keller' and 'Anne Sullivan' in English; spell 'a-i-r' letter by letter (id) and 'w-a-t-e-r' (en).

clips.text: She wrote books and visited 39 countries to speak up for blind people. From Helen we learn never to give up.
clips.note: ST-KELLER panel 5 (sej-k-x). Say 'Helen Keller' and 'Anne Sullivan' in English; spell 'a-i-r' letter by letter (id) and 'w-a-t-e-r' (en).

clips.text: George Washington Carver was born around 1864 in Missouri, in the United States. He was born enslaved, and slavery was abolished while he was a baby.
clips.note: ST-CARVER panel 1 (sej-k-x). Say 'George Washington Carver' and 'Tuskegee' (tus-KEE-gee) in English.

clips.text: He loved plants, and neighbours brought him wilting plants because he knew how to heal them. They called him "the plant doctor".
clips.note: ST-CARVER panel 2 (sej-k-x). Say 'George Washington Carver' and 'Tuskegee' (tus-KEE-gee) in English.

clips.text: Many schools turned him away because of the colour of his skin. He did not give up and kept looking, until at last he studied farming at a college in Iowa.
clips.note: ST-CARVER panel 3 (sej-k-x). Say 'George Washington Carver' and 'Tuskegee' (tus-KEE-gee) in English.

clips.text: In 1896 he became a teacher at Tuskegee, Alabama. He taught farmers to grow peanuts and sweet potatoes in turn with cotton, so the soil stayed rich.
clips.note: ST-CARVER panel 4 (sej-k-x). Say 'George Washington Carver' and 'Tuskegee' (tus-KEE-gee) in English.

clips.text: In his lab he found more than 300 uses for the peanut: soap, ink, oil and more. He also travelled with a wagon school to teach farmers.
clips.note: ST-CARVER panel 5 (sej-k-x). Say 'George Washington Carver' and 'Tuskegee' (tus-KEE-gee) in English.

clips.text: Carver taught for 47 years and gave his knowledge away freely. From Carver we learn to care for the earth and to share what we know.
clips.note: ST-CARVER panel 6 (sej-k-x). Say 'George Washington Carver' and 'Tuskegee' (tus-KEE-gee) in English.

clips.text: Wangari Maathai was born in 1940 in Nyeri, Kenya, at the foot of green mountains. She loved playing by a little stream.
clips.note: ST-MAATHAI panel 1 (sej-k-x). Say 'Wangari Maathai' as wan-GA-ri ma-A-tai; 'Nyeri' as NYE-ri.

clips.text: She studied biology as far as America and Germany. In 1971 she became the first woman in East Africa to earn a doctorate.
clips.note: ST-MAATHAI panel 2 (sej-k-x). Say 'Wangari Maathai' as wan-GA-ri ma-A-tai; 'Nyeri' as NYE-ri.

clips.text: Village mothers told her: the streams were drying up, firewood was farther away and the soil washed away in the rain, because the trees had been cut down.
clips.note: ST-MAATHAI panel 3 (sej-k-x). Say 'Wangari Maathai' as wan-GA-ri ma-A-tai; 'Nyeri' as NYE-ri.

clips.text: In 1977 she started the Green Belt Movement. Mothers grew seedlings and planted trees around their villages.
clips.note: ST-MAATHAI panel 4 (sej-k-x). Say 'Wangari Maathai' as wan-GA-ri ma-A-tai; 'Nyeri' as NYE-ri.

clips.text: Tens of millions of trees grew. In 2004 she won the Nobel Peace Prize, the first African woman to receive it.
clips.note: ST-MAATHAI panel 5 (sej-k-x). Say 'Wangari Maathai' as wan-GA-ri ma-A-tai; 'Nyeri' as NYE-ri.

clips.text: From Wangari we learn that a small act, like planting one tree, can change the world.
clips.note: ST-MAATHAI panel 6 (sej-k-x). Say 'Wangari Maathai' as wan-GA-ri ma-A-tai; 'Nyeri' as NYE-ri.

clips.text: Nelson Mandela was born in 1918 in the village of Mvezo, South Africa. His childhood name was Rolihlahla; his teacher gave him the name Nelson at school.
clips.note: ST-MANDELA panel 1 (sej-k-x). Say 'Rolihlahla' as ro-li-SHLA-shla (approx.), 'Mvezo' as m-VE-zo, 'de Klerk' as de KLERK.

clips.text: In those days, apartheid laws separated people by the colour of their skin. Black people could not vote and were kept out of many places.
clips.note: ST-MANDELA panel 2 (sej-k-x). Say 'Rolihlahla' as ro-li-SHLA-shla (approx.), 'Mvezo' as m-VE-zo, 'de Klerk' as de KLERK.

clips.text: Mandela, a lawyer, demanded that everyone be treated as equals. For that he was imprisoned for 27 years, mostly on Robben Island.
clips.note: ST-MANDELA panel 3 (sej-k-x). Say 'Rolihlahla' as ro-li-SHLA-shla (approx.), 'Mvezo' as m-VE-zo, 'de Klerk' as de KLERK.

clips.text: In prison he kept studying and reading. On 11 February 1990 he was finally free, welcomed by thousands of people.
clips.note: ST-MANDELA panel 4 (sej-k-x). Say 'Rolihlahla' as ro-li-SHLA-shla (approx.), 'Mvezo' as m-VE-zo, 'de Klerk' as de KLERK.

clips.text: He did not seek revenge. He shook hands with his opponents, and with President de Klerk he won the 1993 Nobel Peace Prize.
clips.note: ST-MANDELA panel 5 (sej-k-x). Say 'Rolihlahla' as ro-li-SHLA-shla (approx.), 'Mvezo' as m-VE-zo, 'de Klerk' as de KLERK.

clips.text: In 1994 every citizen could vote for the first time, and Mandela became president. Every 18 July, the world marks Mandela Day by doing good deeds.
clips.note: ST-MANDELA panel 6 (sej-k-x). Say 'Rolihlahla' as ro-li-SHLA-shla (approx.), 'Mvezo' as m-VE-zo, 'de Klerk' as de KLERK.
